turns.t: Doctor, there's a dark curtain coming down over my left eye, I noticed it this morning while I was doing the toast, and I nearly dropped the lot.
Okay, thank you for coming straight in. A dark curtain over the left eye, since this morning. Tell me more about how it looks.
It starts at the top and drifts down, like a blind. My sister had a blind in her kitchen like that, always stuck halfway.
Right. So from the top, going down. Is it still there now?
It is, yes. About a third of the way over, I'd say. I can see around the edges, like looking through a keyhole.
Understood. I'm going to check a couple of things quickly, because this needs looking at properly today. Do you take any regular tablets?
I do, for my high blood pressure. Bisoprolol, maybe 5 mg? I'd have to check the box, to be honest.
No worries. 5 mg, maybe, so we can confirm it later. How often do you take it?
Every morning with my tea. Never miss it. Well, that's not strictly true, the odd morning I forget, usually when the grandchildren are here.
That's very common, so no judgement. Every morning, with a few missed. Now, let me take your pressure and pulse.
Go on. It'll be high, I've been in a state since breakfast.
Your blood pressure is 158/94, and your pulse is 78.
Is that bad?
It's a bit up, which is not a surprise after this morning's fright. We'll come back to it. Now, I'll shine a light into your eyes. Look at the wall for me.
I used to do this at the school, with the nurse, and the lights always made me sneeze.
Just try not to sneeze for me. Both pupils are equal, and they react to light normally.
Grand. Is that good?
That's reassuring. And the front of both eyes looks clear, nice and clean.
I do wash them. My mother always said bathe the eyes in cold tea, can you believe it?
Please don't, not with this. Tell me, apart from the eye, how has the rest of you been? Your general health?
Fine, really. Fit as a fiddle for my age, I walk the dog every day.
Good. Now, I want to be honest with you. I can't tell you from here what is causing this, and I'm not going to guess.
Ah. That sounds serious.
It needs a specialist with the right equipment, and soon. A sudden curtain like yours is something we send to the eye hospital the same day.
Today? I've the dog in the car.
Today, yes. I'll write a letter and send you straight to the eye casualty at the hospital. Can someone drive you?
My neighbour's outside, he gave me the lift. Thomas, a lovely man, he does the bins as well.
Perfect. Please don't drive yourself, and don't wait until later this afternoon.
Right. And the dog?
Thomas can take the dog home first, if he's quick. But you go on to the hospital straight after that.
I will. Honestly, I thought it'd be a drop of something and home for lunch.
I know. So, just to repeat it: the left eye, a dark curtain since this morning, and you're going to the eye hospital today with my letter.
Eye hospital, today, with the letter. Got it.
Good. They'll take over from here. Mind yourself, and tell them everything you've told me.
I will. Thanks, doctor. God bless.

Do not drive yourself; go to the hospital straight away

Patient says she takes it every morning but also admits forgetting some mornings.
